commit.message:
Auto-finalize tapKeySig-only Taproot inputs on PSBT v2 extract

When NIP-07 sends a BIP-375 silent-payment PSBT to a signer, the signer
follows BIP-174's split between 'signed' and 'finalized': it records
the Schnorr signature in PSBT_IN_TAP_KEY_SIG (0x13) and leaves the
finalizing step (wrapping that signature into a single-item witness
stack per BIP-341 §'Validation') to a separate Finalizer role.

Ditto's wallet was treating that PSBT shape as un-finalized and
refusing to extract it with 'input N is not finalized (no scriptSig or
witness)'. Symptom in the UI: send to an sp1… address via NIP-07
fails at the extraction step.

The parser now surfaces tapKeySig on ParsedPsbtV2Input, and
extractTxFromSignedPsbtV2 auto-finalizes Taproot key-path inputs by
setting finalScriptWitness = [tapKeySig] before the on-the-wire checks.
That's what @scure/btc-signer's own finalizeIdx does for taproot
key-path spends.

The local NSecSignerBtc path is unaffected — it already calls
tx.finalize() before re-emitting the PSBT v2, so finalScriptWitness is
populated and the new auto-finalize branch is inert. This is the first
end-to-end NIP-07 SP send the extractor has actually seen — the latent
bug has been in the silent-payment path since it was introduced in
9be302e9.

commit.message:
Attach BIP-375 ECDH share + DLEQ proof to signed SP PSBTs

The local nsec signer was previously resolving silent-payment outputs
to concrete P2TR scripts and signing — correct on-chain, but the
finalized PSBT carried no proof that the resolution was honest. Any
external BIP-375 verifier inspecting the signed PSBT would see the
output scripts but no PSBT_GLOBAL_SP_ECDH_SHARE / PSBT_GLOBAL_SP_DLEQ
rows tying them to the input keys; the resolution had to be taken on
faith.

Now the signer:

  - aggregates the senders' tweaked private keys with
    aggregateSenderPrivateKey() (already in silentPayments.ts),
  - computes C = a \u00b7 B_scan per recipient scan key with
    computeBip375EcdhShare(),
  - generates the matching BIP-374 DLEQ proof with the new dleq.ts
    primitive (verified against the canonical
    bip374_{generate,verify}_proof.csv test vectors \u2014 28 cases),
  - emits one PSBT_GLOBAL_SP_ECDH_SHARE + PSBT_GLOBAL_SP_DLEQ pair per
    scan key (keyed by the 33-byte scan key, per the spec), and
  - clears PSBT_GLOBAL_TX_MODIFIABLE to 0 as BIP-375 requires once
    every output script has been written.

A new silentPaymentGlobals option on encodePsbtV2 carries this through.
The 311-test suite still passes (and the existing BIP-375 fast-path
test exercises the new code path).

dleq.ts is adapted from the equivalent module in ditto-extension, with
the @noble/curves v1 / v2 API translated (schnorr.Point \u2192
secp256k1.ProjectivePoint, .toBytes \u2192 .toRawBytes, P.is0() \u2192
P.equals(POINT_ZERO)) to match the rest of the codebase, and the
jsdom-realm taggedHash workaround applied.

commit.message:
Back psbtV2 codec with @scure/btc-signer's _RawPSBTV2

The previous implementation was a hand-rolled PSBTv2 + BIP-375 encoder
and parser — ~705 lines walking bytes by hand. It also forced the local
nsec signer to splice PSBT_IN_FINAL_SCRIPTWITNESS rows into the encoded
PSBT after the fact (encodePsbtV2WithWitnesses, ~140 lines of post-hoc
byte surgery) because the public encoder couldn't emit them.

Delegating to the library's internal _RawPSBTV2 coder removes both
piles of code: the magic/framing/varint/per-field-codec work is now the
library's job, and the encoder accepts a finalScriptWitness on
PsbtV2Input directly. The library's _RawPSBTV2 (vs. its more strict
RawPSBTV2 used by Transaction) leaves PSBT_OUT_SCRIPT optional on
outputs that only carry PSBT_OUT_SP_V0_INFO — exactly the property
BIP-375 needs from a constructor-side codec.

The public API (encodePsbtV2 / parsePsbtV2 /
extractTxFromSignedPsbtV2 / encodeCompactSize / PsbtV2Input / etc.) is
unchanged; only the internals were rewired. The full PSBTv2 + bitcoin
test suites pass without modification.

One library-error message swap: PSBT v0 input now hits a sniff in our
own decoder before being handed off, so the error wording stays the
project's familiar 'only PSBT v2 is supported' instead of the
library's internal 'PSBTv0: missing unsignedTx'.

commit.message:
Adopt ditto-extension's silentPayments.ts superset

The decoder half of the two files was already identical; this picks up
the full BIP-352 sender derivation (multi-recipient grouping by scan
key, input-eligibility matrix with NUMS-H detection, K_max checks), the
BIP-375 ECDH-share helpers (aggregateSenderPrivateKey,
computeBip375EcdhShare, deriveSPOutputScriptFromShare),
encodeSilentPaymentAddress, p2trScriptPubKey, and tweakNsecForTaproot.

The new derivation is verified against the canonical
send_and_receive_test_vectors.json from BIP-352; all 27 sender vectors
now pass.

Internal differences from the extension's copy:

- @noble/curves v1 / @noble/hashes v1 imports (matches the rest of the
  codebase); Point.fromBytes -> Point.fromHex, .toBytes -> .toRawBytes,
  P.is0() replaced with an affine point-at-infinity check.
- taggedHash copies its TextEncoder output into a fresh Uint8Array to
  dodge the jsdom-realm prototype mismatch noble's u8a check trips on.
- validateSilentPaymentAddress (already used in SendBitcoinDialog) kept
  as a thin try/catch around decodeSilentPaymentAddress.

NSecSignerBtc's BIP-375 fast path is rewritten to use
deriveSilentPaymentOutputs, which handles all recipients in a single
call and groups them correctly by scan key. The old bespoke single-
recipient helper (deriveSilentPaymentOutputScript) is gone.

Also bumps the BTC price query's staleTime from 30s to 60s so the
wallet page stops refetching on every mount while mempool.space's
underlying feed only refreshes once a minute.

commit.message:
Replace bitcoinjs-lib with @scure/btc-signer

Drops bitcoinjs-lib, ecpair, @bitcoinerlab/secp256k1, and the buffer
polyfill in favor of @scure/btc-signer + @noble/curves. The new stack
is pure-Uint8Array (no Node Buffer), audited, and ~5x smaller.

P2TR address derivation, PSBT construction, local Schnorr signing, and
finalization all run through @scure/btc-signer. Existing P2TR address
regression fixtures pass unchanged, confirming byte-for-byte parity
with the previous derivation.

commit.message:
Scan QR codes for wallet Send recipient

Add a camera button inside the recipient input of the wallet's Send
dialog. Tapping it opens a live QR scanner that reads on-chain
addresses, BIP-21 `bitcoin:` URIs, and Nostr identifiers
(npub/nprofile/nip05/hex, with or without a `nostr:` prefix).
Bitcoin addresses select directly; Nostr identifiers are routed
through the existing dropdown for one-tap confirmation.

Uses the `qr-scanner` library (`getUserMedia` + ZXing/BarcodeDetector
under the hood), keeping a single implementation across web,
WKWebView, and Android WebView. The native @capacitor-mlkit plugin
would have been faster but only supports CocoaPods on iOS, which
Ditto's SPM-based project can't use.

The dialog uses a callback ref on the <video> element instead of
`useRef`. Radix Dialog mounts DialogContent lazily through a Portal,
so a plain ref is null on the first effect tick after `isOpen` flips
true \u2014 the scanner would then bail before construction and the
user would see a silent black square. The callback ref re-runs the
effect once the element actually attaches.

Other defensive measures (each turns a silent failure into a readable
error instead of a black screen):

  - Secure-context and `mediaDevices` feature guards up front.
  - A 6-second readiness watchdog. If `start()` neither resolves nor
    rejects, or resolves but the video never reaches HAVE_METADATA,
    flip to an error state.
  - Retry once without `facingMode: 'environment'` on
    OverconstrainedError (laptops without rear cameras, locked-down
    WebViews).
  - Wider error mapping: NotReadableError, SecurityError, and
    OverconstrainedError now produce actionable messages.

Dialog sizing is constrained so it never escapes the viewport: width
caps at `min(380px, 100vw-2rem)`, height at `100svh-2rem` (using
small-viewport-height to avoid iOS Safari address-bar shift), and the
square video container caps its own height to match its width.

CSP gets two new directives so qr-scanner's blob-backed decoder
worker (used as a fallback on devices without BarcodeDetector) can
construct: `worker-src 'self' blob:; child-src 'self' blob:`. The
grant is narrow \u2014 same-origin scripts and blob URLs only, no
wildcard widening of `script-src`. `child-src` is included as a
fallback for older browsers that haven't implemented `worker-src`.

Android gains the `CAMERA` permission needed by WebView's
`getUserMedia`. iOS `NSCameraUsageDescription` was already present.

commit.message:
Add Bitcoin APIs editor to Wallet settings

Surfaces `esploraApis` in Settings > Advanced > Wallet (and on the dedicated
/settings/wallet route, which renders the same WalletSettings component).
Users can add HTTPS Esplora roots, reorder them to control the failover
priority, remove individual endpoints, and restore the default list of
mempool.space -> mempool.emzy.de -> blockstream.info.

Removal is blocked when only one endpoint remains, matching the Zod
schema's .min(1) constraint. The default list is now exported from
src/lib/esplora.ts as DEFAULT_ESPLORA_APIS so App.tsx (default config) and
the settings UI (restore button + diff check) share a single source of
truth.

commit.message:
Esplora REST failover with abort signals and timeouts

Replace the single `esploraBaseUrl: string` with `esploraApis: string[]`
and route every Esplora REST call through a new `esploraFetch` helper
that handles ordered failover across multiple API endpoints.

The failover client:

- Tries URLs in order with a per-attempt 15s timeout. mempool.space has
  a shadowban-style rate-limit behaviour where requests are silently
  absorbed and never reply; the timeout converts that hang into a
  regular failover signal so the next URL is tried.
- On `429` / `5xx` / network error / timeout, parks the URL in a
  module-level cool-down with exponential backoff (30s, 60s, 120s,
  240s, 300s cap) and advances to the next.
- Resets a URL's failure count on the first 2xx response, so the
  primary comes back into rotation as soon as it recovers.
- Treats configurable `skipStatuses` (e.g. `404` on `/v1/prices`) as
  endpoint-capability mismatches: skip without penalising the endpoint.
  This lets non-mempool backends like Blockstream coexist in the list
  even though they don't expose the price extension.
- Composes a caller-supplied AbortSignal with the per-attempt timeout
  via AbortSignal.any. Caller aborts (e.g. TanStack Query queryFn
  unmounts) propagate immediately; timeouts mark the endpoint failed
  and try the next URL.
- Falls back to cooled-down endpoints when *every* URL is in cool-down,
  rather than failing outright.

Default list is mempool.space -> mempool.emzy.de -> blockstream.info.

Every Esplora-touching helper in `src/lib/bitcoin.ts` (plus
`verifyOnchainZap` in `useOnchainZaps`) now takes
`(input, esploraApis: string[], signal?: AbortSignal)`. TanStack Query
callers thread their `queryFn` signal through; broadcast mutations call
without an explicit signal but still get the 15s per-attempt timeout.
